I’m a computational neuroscientist working on the mechanisms of intelligence. I try to understand how the brain forms internal representations of the world and uses them for sophisticated feats of cognition, like planning and decision-making.
I’m currently a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Oxford with Thomas Akam. Together with collaborators at Oxford and the Sainsbury Wellcome Centre, we’re using reinforcement learning theory to study how the brain might support goal-directed behaviour over long time horizons. You can read more about this here.
I completed a DPhil (2020–24) and MSc in Experimental Psychology (2018–19) as a Clarendon Scholar at Oxford with Matthew Rushworth and Nima Khalighinejad. Before that, I studied Philosophy and Psychology as an undergraduate at the University of Sydney, where I was awarded the University Medal. I focused on Wittgenstein, Kant, and post-Kantian German Idealism. These ideas continue to influence my thinking.
Outside academia, I was a Fellow at Artis Ventures (2024–25) in San Francisco, where I covered neurotechnology startups enabled by advances in machine learning and brain–machine interfaces. I remain interested in how new technologies might help us understand the brain, and, reciprocally, in how insights from neuroscience might inform new technologies.
